summary: 1914 guyed 60-foot fire tower first erected elsewhere, moved twice, at Ross Mountain since the 1940s; no longer in active use, kept by Maine Forest Service.

facts.design: Guyed 60-foot tower with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab; first erected in 1914 at another location
facts.status_note: No longer in active use; maintained by the Maine Forest Service for emergency detection

events.note: First erected at another location, per the Register; the Register's build year is 1914 for the first site
Moved to its present site. The tower has been moved twice; the Register gives only 'the 1940s' for the present site, so the year shown stands for the decade
Registered May 30, 1996 as US 170, ME 8; nominated by Bob Spear, FFLA

notes_for_editor: No source read gives staffing, fire history, or public access for this tower, so no access or staffing key is recorded. The brief's 1914 build date refers to the first site; the present site dates only to the 1940s. Registration date confirmed on the NHLR page. A social-media photo caption was seen but not used because it is not a citable source. Brief coordinates differ slightly from the FLO list (46.54703, -69.76447); not material.
